notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates are nearly always fully red, the only country in Asia to do this.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Coverage is a grey car with no antenna, the only grey Google car in a left-driving country.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Stone blocks serve as safety barriers on winding rural roads and are one of the best rural clues; guardrails are rare.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Traditional houses have tin roofs and painted wooden frames, a very distinctive look.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The local script has unique-looking letters found nowhere else on Street View.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very mountainous, with most coverage on mountain roads; only the south is flat.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Prayer flags are often seen beside the road.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Thin metal poles occasionally appear, often painted black at the bottom.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road markers have a yellow top and white bottom; on highways the road number is on top.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Town signs are often red or blue and carry the name of the town.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Taxis have yellow plates and yellow roofs.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Signposts often have black-and-white stripes; seen also in Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Malaysia and Bangladesh.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Two solid white edge lines appear only in the west, south of the capital.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat land with no mountains in view exists only in the south, which has limited coverage.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The Phobjikha Valley is a wide, fairly flat farming valley with no big river, the largest open valley on Street View.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A hook can be seen on the back of the car in Haa District.
